0.title: Interactive Sync Review & Deletion Diff Visualizer
0.content: Standard automated sync daemons run unattended in background crons. When an unexpected deletion wave occurs—such as an operator accidentally moving a root directory or an external service wiping a folder—unattended sync immediately replicates the wipe across all replicas. Bisync Hub introduces an interactive human-in-the-loop inspection barrier before destructive mutations are committed.

1.title: How It Works
1.content: [ Trigger Sync ] ──► [ Dry-Run Operation ] ──► [ Parse Mutation List ] │ ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ Deletions <= Max Threshold Deletions > Max Threshold │ │ ▼ ▼ [ Auto-Apply Policies ] [ HALT & Emit Review Event ] │ ▼ [ Operator Decision Modal ] • Confirm Specific Deletes • Reject / Abort Run • Override Heuristics .

2.title: 1. Dry-Run Mutation Analysis
2.content: Every scheduled or manual sync cycle executes in --dry-run inspection mode first. The engine streams the stdout/stderr mutation log and categorizes every proposed operation: . | + CREATE: New file appearing on either Path1 or Path2. | ~ MODIFY: Content or metadata discrepancy requiring replication. | - DELETE: Proposed removal of a file or directory. | .

3.title: 2. High-Severity Quota Halts
3.content: If proposed deletions exceed either: . | The absolute file limit (e.g. MAX_DELETE_COUNT=50), or | The directory percentage ratio (e.g. MAX_DELETE_PERCENT=10%), | . the sync engine immediately trips the circuit breaker, writes an atomic .review_pending state, and emits real-time WebSocket notifications to the management dashboard.

4.title: 3. Granular Operator Triage
4.content: Operators can open the Web Dashboard review modal to: . | Inspect file diffs, file sizes, and last modified timestamps side-by-side. | Selectively whitelist legitimate bulk deletions while rejecting questionable removals. | Commit the approved batch or abort the run cleanly without leaving locks in place. | . Safety Guarantee: No file is ever removed when a review threshold is tripped until an authorized operator explicitly signs off or an automated timeout policy executes an abort.

6.title: Multi-Analyzer Heuristic Conflict Engine
6.content: Most bidirectional sync tools rely on a naive, binary rule: “newer timestamp wins”. In distributed cloud environments, this rule causes silent data loss because: . | Cloud storage APIs (e.g. Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, SharePoint) round timestamps to 1-second or 2-second windows or update them asynchronously. | Device clocks can drift or suffer skew during daylight savings transitions. | Rapid concurrent edits on mobile and desktop produce collisions where the “newer” file is actually an incomplete draft. | . Bisync Hub replaces timestamp gambling with a multi-analyzer heuristic confidence engine.

7.title: The Evaluation Pipeline
7.content: When both Path1 and Path2 report modifications to the same file path, the engine executes four independent heuristic analyzers: . | Heuristic Analyzer | Signal Analyzed | Weight | Description | . | SizeDivergenceAnalyzer | Content volume delta | 30% | Detects dramatic file shrinks or expansions indicating truncation or major additions. | . | BinarySignatureAnalyzer | MIME & header magic bytes | 25% | Verifies format validity (e.g. SQLite database header, JPEG signatures) to penalize corrupt partial writes. | . | ClockSkewAnalyzer | Cross-remote timestamp drift | 25% | Evaluates cloud API timestamp granularity and compensates for known provider skews (e.g., OneDrive 2s window). | . | VelocityAnalyzer | Modification frequency | 20% | Scores edit frequency to distinguish steady active editing from stale background touches. | .

8.title: Confidence Calculation & Safety Bands
8.content: The engine aggregates individual analyzer scores into a unified Confidence Index (0% - 100%): . Score >= 85% ──► [ HIGH CONFIDENCE ] ──► Auto-resolve in favor of dominant replica 60% - 84% ──► [ MEDIUM CONFIDENCE ]──► Backup losing candidate to .conflict-bak, then sync Score < 60% ──► [ LOW CONFIDENCE ] ──► QUARANTINE: Halt file mutation & prompt Operator .

9.title: Safety Features
9.content: . | Deterministic Quarantine: Unresolvable collisions are safely preserved in a .bisync_quarantine/ isolation jail. | Conflict Backup Preserves: Even on high-confidence resolutions, the displaced version is moved to the backup store before overwriting. | Clock Skew Tolerance: Built-in compensation algorithms for cloud timestamp drift and DST shifts. | . All heuristic scoring weights and confidence thresholds are fully configurable in bisync.env to match your organization’s risk tolerance.

11.title: Customizable Safety Policies & Circuit Breakers
11.content: ◆ Planned Milestone (Near-Term Priority #2) . Roadmap Specification: The customizable two-stage safety policy engine and declarative circuit breakers described below are fully specified in Safety Policies Design Specification and scheduled for implementation following the Immutable Audit Ledger. Automated tools must know when to stop. Running bidirectional synchronization when a network share is unmounted, when a cloud provider returns HTTP 429 rate limits, or when a disk is failing will corrupt sync state and trigger cascading deletions. Bisync Hub implements a two-stage defensive policy barrier: Pre-Execution and Pre-Mutation.

13.title: 1. Pre-Execution Validation Gates
13.content: Before invoking any sync or check command, Bisync Hub checks environmental invariants: . | Canary File Verification (RCLONE_TEST): . | Requires a known marker file to exist on both local and remote mount roots. | If a network volume unmounts or cloud sync token expires, the canary file disappears. The engine detects this and aborts instantly, preventing the empty directory from being treated as a mass deletion. | . | Path Confinement (Filesystem Jail): . | All local file manipulations are strictly validated with filepath.Rel and prefix checks to ensure zero path traversal escapes outside designated sync roots. | . | Advisory POSIX Locking (flock): . | Prevents overlapping sync jobs from corrupting local metadata or triggering race conditions across systemd timers or manual CLI runs. | . | .

14.title: 2. Pre-Mutation Circuit Breakers
14.content: During sync execution, incoming mutation requests pass through configurable circuit breakers: . # bisync.env safety settings SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_COUNT=25 # Hard limit on total file removals per run SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_RATIO=0.10 # Maximum 10% of total files may be deleted SAFETY_ENABLE_CANARY=true # Canary file mandatory on both remotes SAFETY_RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF=true # Exponential backoff on provider HTTP 429 .

15.title: 3. Automatic Backoff & Quarantine
15.content: . | Provider Throttling: When Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive signals rate limits (429 Too Many Requests), Bisync Hub immediately halts further calls and enforces exponential backoff with jitter. | Fail-Safe Abort: Any violation of a safety policy halts execution cleanly and logs the event to the audit ledger. | . Zero Canary Bypass Policy: Canary check routines are hardcoded to fail-closed. If canary status is ambiguous, sync execution is blocked.

17.title: Cryptographic Immutable Audit Ledger
17.content: ◆ Planned Milestone (Near-Term Priority #1) . Roadmap Specification: The Cryptographic Immutable Audit Ledger detailed below represents Near-Term Strategic Priority #1 on our development roadmap. The schema architecture, SQLite trigger design, and verification tooling are ready for immediate implementation post-public launch. Compliance, security audits, and forensic debugging require an undeniable, tamper-evident record of all storage mutations: Who deleted file X? When was conflict Y resolved? What was the decision confidence score? . Bisync Hub embeds an immutable, SQLite-backed cryptographic ledger with trigger-enforced append-only constraints.

19.title: 1. SQLite Trigger-Enforced Immutability
19.content: The internal SQLite database employs schema-level BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers on audit tables: . CREATE TRIGGER prevent_ledger_tampering BEFORE UPDATE ON audit_events BEGIN SELECT RAISE(FAIL, 'FATAL: audit_events table is strictly append-only.'); END; . Even if an attacker or misconfigured script gains write access to the database file, existing audit entries cannot be modified or purged without breaking database integrity.

20.title: 2. SHA-256 Hash Chaining
20.content: Each audit entry computes a SHA-256 digest over the concatenation of: . | Previous_Record_Hash | Event_Type and Timestamp (UTC millisecond precision) | Payload_JSON (redacted secrets, sanitized paths, decision scores) | . The application provides a built-in cryptographic verification command (bisync-hub verify-ledger) to audit chain integrity and identify any external byte tampering.

21.title: 3. Redaction by Default
21.content: All sensitive credentials—including RC_PASS, OAuth refresh tokens, webhook URLs, and private auth headers—are recursively redacted via security.RedactSecrets before entering the audit stream. The audit ledger ensures full compliance with operational standards while protecting organizational data sovereignty.

26.title: 2. POSIX Flocking & Atomic File Writes
26.content: Process concurrency and state isolation rely entirely on OS-native POSIX advisory locks (syscall.Flock). | Zero reliance on external lock daemons (Redis / Zookeeper). | State persistence and telemetry use atomic rename semantics (.tmp.<pid> + os.Rename) to prevent half-written files during sudden power loss or server restarts. | .

27.title: 3. Multi-Platform Cross-Compilation
27.content: Compiles cleanly across modern platforms with standard Go tooling: . | linux/amd64 (Standard servers & workstations) | linux/arm64 (Raspberry Pi, AWS Graviton, Apple Silicon Linux VMs) | darwin/amd64 & darwin/arm64 (macOS workstations) | . You can deploy Bisync Hub to an edge Raspberry Pi, a corporate Linux server, or a NAS box with a single scp command.

29.title: Architecture & Safety Principles
29.content: Bisync Hub is designed under the assumption that networks drop, cloud APIs produce unexpected HTTP responses, and distributed clocks drift. Every design decision adheres to three foundational tenets: . | Visibility Before Action: Never mutate remote storage silently without an immutable record and pre-flight inspection. | Safety Before Automation: If an environmental invariant is violated (e.g. missing canary, unresolvable conflict), halt immediately rather than guess. | Defense in Depth: Protect the host filesystem with path confinement jails, POSIX process flocking, and secret scrubbing. | .

31.title: 1. Filesystem Path Confinement Jails
31.content: When browsing files or preparing sync operations on local storage endpoints, Bisync Hub prevents arbitrary filesystem access by enforcing strict jail boundaries: . // Enforcing local path isolation relPath, err := filepath.Rel(jailRoot, targetPath) if err != nil || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, "..") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, "/") { return ErrPathTraversalViolation } . Any request attempting directory traversal (../) outside the configured root returns an immediate authorization violation and is recorded in the audit log.

32.title: 2. POSIX Flock Process Isolation
32.content: To avoid lock races between scheduled background timers, cron jobs, and interactive operator CLI requests, Bisync Hub acquires advisory file locks using native POSIX flock(fd, LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB). | Concurrent executions fail fast with a clear error rather than piling up or corrupting state. | Stale lock detection cleans up safely if a previous process terminated abnormally. | .

33.title: 3. Secret Redaction at Every Boundary
33.content: All external inputs, configuration files, and API logs pass through recursive sanitization via security.RedactSecrets. | Keywords matching PASS, TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, and CREDENTIAL are dynamically masked ([REDACTED]). | Raw tokens are never persisted in SQLite ledger records, JSON error messages, or telemetry streams. | .

34.title: 4. Zero-Exposure CI/CD Security
34.content: Bisync Hub’s GitHub Actions pipelines are deployed 100% on cloud-hosted ephemeral runners (ubuntu-latest) with zero self-hosted runner exposure. Every commit is validated with: . | Static analysis via go vet | Automated leak scanning via gitleaks | Vulnerability auditing via govulncheck | Strict branch protection with sole review governance (@slemmercs) | .

37.title: Why Not Just Run a Cron Script?
37.content: Cron scripts are ubiquitous, but they fail silently when edge cases occur: . | The Unmounted Mount Disaster: If an NFS/SMB share or rclone mount disconnects, an automated cron script sees an empty folder and issues deletions for thousands of files across the remote replica. | The Cloud Timestamp Shift: Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive report timestamps differently than local ext4/APFS filesystems. A simple script relying on test fileA -nt fileB frequently overwrites valid changes. | Overlapping Job Corruption: If a sync run takes longer than the cron interval (e.g., due to large video uploads), concurrent sync instances access the cache simultaneously, corrupting .bisync lock state. | . Bisync Hub eliminates every one of these failure modes out of the box.

50.title: The Bidirectional Dilemma
50.content: Standard bidirectional synchronization tools face a fundamental challenge: How do you reconcile silent file deletions and conflicting concurrent edits without risking catastrophic data loss? . 59.title: Quickstart Guide
59.content: Get up and running with Bisync Hub in less than 5 minutes.

60.title: 1. Quick Installation
60.content: Execute the automated installer to download the latest signed binary and setup basic system integration: . curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slemmercs/rclone-bisync/main/deploy/install.sh | bash .

61.title: Manual Binary Download
61.content: Alternatively, download the target binary directly from GitHub Releases: . # Example for Linux x86_64 curl -LO https://github.com/slemmercs/rclone-bisync/releases/latest/download/bisync-hub-linux-amd64 chmod +x bisync-hub-linux-amd64 sudo mv bisync-hub-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/bisync-hub .

62.title: 2. Configuration (bisync.env)
62.content: Generate a starting configuration or customize bisync.env in your working directory: . # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ # Bisync Hub Core Configuration # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ PORT=8080 BIND_ADDR=127.0.0.1 # Sync Paths PATH1=/home/operator/data PATH2=onedrive:data_backup # Safety & Circuit Breakers SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_COUNT=25 SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_RATIO=0.10 SAFETY_ENABLE_CANARY=true CANARY_FILENAME=RCLONE_TEST # Conflict Engine Settings CONFLICT_AUTO_RESOLVE_MIN_CONFIDENCE=0.85 CONFLICT_BACKUP_LOSERS=true # Notification Webhooks (Planned Roadmap Feature) # DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL= # TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN= # TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID= # HEALTHCHECKS_URL= .

63.title: 3. Starting the Server
63.content: Run the orchestrator interactively: . bisync-hub --config bisync.env . Open your browser to http://localhost:8080 to access the real-time operational dashboard, inspect remote mounts, check canary health, and review pending sync events. Storage Remotes Remote health checks & OAuth indicators Dual-Pane Explorer Browse local and remote directories .

64.title: 4. Running as a Systemd Service
64.content: For continuous 24/7 background operation on Linux: . # /etc/systemd/system/bisync-hub.service [Unit] Description=Bisync Hub Cloud Orchestrator After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target [Service] Type=simple User=csaba WorkingDirectory=/home/csaba/sync ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/bisync-hub --config /home/csaba/sync/bisync.env Restart=always RestartSec=10 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target . Enable and start the service: . sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now bisync-hub .
